scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8142: Since the maintenance visit to the Campus 2 access
switch, people on both of our floors -- the 10.5.0.x group and the
10.6.0.x group -- cannot reach their usual way out of the floor. Both
groups at once, straight after your maintenance: that is not a
coincidence, that is the maintenance. The person who reported it to me
already called it: "one of the VLANs probably fell off the trunk". I have
no idea what that means and I do not need to -- your visit broke it, your
team puts it back. Check what the maintenance left out and restore it
today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. switch4's trunk to sshswitch carries both
  VLAN 5 and VLAN 6, and both forward: VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach
  10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach 10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  trunk/VLAN-pruning fault on switch4 that is not occurring (cf.
  kath4-switch4-trunk-vlan5-down, where the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- switch4's trunk dropping
VLAN 5 or VLAN 6 so hosts lose their uplink -- is NOT reproducible: both VLANs
forward over the trunk. PC1 (VLAN 5) reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss and PC3
(VLAN 6) reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss, confirming both VLANs traverse switch4
to sshswitch.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: switch4's trunk carries both VLANs and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN 5 and
VLAN 6 host->gateway paths, finds both working, checks that switch4's trunk
subinterfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a pruned/dropped
VLAN -- blaming switch4's trunk to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce any outage on the 10.5.0.x (VLAN 5) or 10.6.0.x (VLAN 6) segments, nor find a trunk/VLAN misconfiguration. End-hosts on both floors reach their gateway and the uplink.

Evidence:
- From a 10.5 host (pc2), the default gateway 10.5.0.254 on sshswitch responds and the uplink router (55.5.1.1) is reachable: pc2 -> 10.5.0.254 OK; pc2 -> 55.5.1.1 OK.
- From a 10.6 host (pc3), the default gateway 10.6.0.254 and 55.5.1.1 are reachable: pc3 -> 10.6.0.254 OK; pc3 -> 55.5.1.1 OK.
- The Campus 2 access switch (switch4) has the trunk on eth0 with tagged subinterfaces for VLANs 5 and 6 up and bridged (eth0.5 -> br_vlan5, eth0.6 -> br_vlan6), and access ports mapped correctly (eth1-3 in VLAN 5, eth4-5 in VLAN 6).
- The aggregation switch (sshswitch) has corresponding VLAN interfaces up (eth0.5/eth0.6 bridged to br_v5/br_v6), SVIs with 10.5.0.254/10.6.0.254, and OSPF learned routes via br_v1 toward 55.5.1.1 (router17).

Mechanism: If a VLAN had “fallen off” the trunk, hosts would fail to reach 10.5.0.254/10.6.0.254. Instead, both floors’ hosts reach their gateways and the upstream, so the trunk and SVIs are intact.

Localization: No failing interface or process found; switch4.eth0 and sshswitch.eth0/.5/.6 are correctly carrying VLANs 5 and 6.

Root cause: No persistent misconfiguration present; the reported incident was likely a transient effect during maintenance (e.g., brief trunk flap or ARP/STP reconvergence).

Corrective fix: No change required. If issues recur, verify ms1_sw4 trunk allows VLANs 5 and 6 on both ends and consider scheduling a short maintenance window to audit/standardize trunk native/allowed VLANs.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes switch4's trunk carries both VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 and both gateways are reachable with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms switch4.eth0 has VLAN 5 and 6 subinterfaces up and that hosts on both VLANs can reach their gateways and upstream (pings 'OK'), demonstrating the trunk carries both VLANs and a healthy baseline.
